\[
\begin{gathered}
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = A\, I(x,y) - (G_{\sigma} \star I)(x,y)
= (A - 1)\, I(x,y) + \big(I - G_{\sigma} \star I\big)(x,y),
\\[4pt]
A = 2, \quad \sigma = 2
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \(A\): Boost factor, at least 1
- \(G_{\sigma}\): Normalized Gaussian kernel with radius floor(3 sigma + 0.5)
- \(\star\): Correlation
- \(\sigma\): Standard deviation of the Gaussian in pixels

The second form shows what happens: the image is kept with weight A - 1, and the detail that the blur removes is added on top. With A = 1 only the detail is left. With A = 2 the result is the unsharp mask with amount 1. A flat area of value v becomes (A - 1) v, so A above 2 also brightens the image.
